title: Customer-care sentiment: stay feedback and staff interaction

definition.principle: customer-care sentiment has two distinct listening objects; never merge them: route first, then score

route.stay_feedback: a coordinator interviewing an inpatient or attender about the hospital stay
route.staff_interaction: a staff-handled live patient or party task (floor, outpatient, front desk, inpatient, pharmacy, lab, sales) captured on a wearable or similar
route.unscorable: purely internal operations with no patient party, empty or inaudible transcript, or insufficient evidence: unscorable, not satisfied and not a blank scored as zero

layer_A_stay_feedback.object: patient or attender sentiment about the stay, not the coordinator

axes.issue_rule: each object needs supporting evidence; no evidence, no object
axes.concrete_vs_vague: a named missing item is concrete; empty praise after a leading prompt is not
axes.coordinator_leading: a prompted yes is marked and is not valence

severity_of_stay_issues.high: safety risk, blocked care, or an unresolved major service failure

layer_B_staff_interaction.object: quality of the staff-patient or staff-party interaction, not stay valence

quality_band.driven_by: the number of checklist items passed
quality_band.hard_floor_1: safety risk, blocked necessary care or an egregious failure overrides the checklist

checklist.understanding: the need was correctly identified with no misread backtracking
checklist.owning: one person owns it start to finish, or there is an explicit handoff; never a silent drop
checklist.accurate_complete: correct and nothing material left out
checklist.proactive: a specific next step or time offered without being asked
checklist.closed: the other party clearly knows what happens next

band_map.5: all five pass plus a genuine extra

do_not: score care-staff conversations with the consult rubrics
read a quality band as severity or severity as a quality band
rank a coordinator as if a doctor
